decisions.summary: The first house is offered the free ground nearest the seat (capacity.free_seats through the seat region, at most DRY_SPELL offers)
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1: US1 puts the first house at the seed point and the placer decides; one house, not FR-007's exhaustive pass.

decisions.summary: Every standing house offers seats in a jittered ring (+/-12 deg, up to +12%) at the distance where the footprints part plus GROW_GAP - stated at plan line 58 as 'GROW_GAP (6 px)'
decisions.why: Line 58 still states the gap as 6 px, the value round 1 ruled NOT LEGITIMATE because it leaves no room for the path out; line 64 states the fixed value (a corridor's whole strip plus 2 px, 16 px at the reference scale; growth.py grow_gap computes 2 x px(ACCESS_HALF_FT) + 2 = 16.0, measured here). The plan states both, and the stale one is the rejected narrowing. Fix: line 58 says 'plus GROW_GAP (a corridor's whole strip plus 2 px, below)' and drops '6 px'.

decisions.summary: A standing homestead's footprint: envelope, reserved woodlot seats, the south reach of the yard's AND beds' south edges plus SUN_CORRIDOR_FT + 2 ft; the path out as GROW_GAP; the new household's reach the envelope of the LARGEST homestead the roll can take (_bundle_envelope at _house_max)
decisions.why: Two of round 1's three items are fixed and confirmed: the path out (GROW_GAP = the corridor's strip + 2 px) and the garden shade (the beds' south edges + SUN_CORRIDOR_FT + 2 ft, the reach _gardens_sun_ok measures, fit.py:722). The third is not. The plan says the new household's reach is 'the envelope of the LARGEST homestead the roll can take' and that so 'no seat is offered closer than the household's own footprint allows'. That premise was not measured, and it is false. _bundle_envelope at _house_max is the largest HOUSE, but the yard and bed rolls key on the position, and the prototype and growth.py take them at house 0's position only. Measured here (300 positions, _house_max, shed=True): the envelope's west reach runs 140.0-172.1 px and its south reach 60.2-100.5 px, while east (79.9) and north (106.8) are constant. So house 0's envelope is one draw, and a later household can reach up to 40 px further south and 32 px further west than the distance offered for it. That is FR-004's 'never closer than FR-003's distance' unmet, and exactly the 'proxy shown to be the largest' round 1 asked for. Fix: the new household's reach on each side is the MAXIMUM the roll can produce (computed from the yard and bed distributions' bounds, or the per-side maximum over the roll's extremes), or the envelope rolled for that household at the candidate seat. Then state the measurement that shows it is never smaller than any household's envelope. (Checked and NOT a finding: the new household's own sun is not in its reach, but a seat grown north is held off by the standing envelope's north reach, which is 91 px past the house wall against a 41 ft corridor. On seeds 1, 25 and 4 the north sector drew 0 sun_corridor and 0 yard_grove refusals, measured here on the clone's growth.py.)

One of the two is wrong, so correct it to the measured figure.
